text:
maria: Ran a rotary-scale (sigma) sweep across Llama/Mistral/Mixtral/Qwen variants this morning. Targets: linear / NTK / YARN paramizations, longctx stability (up to 32k). Posting quick notes and a small perf table — want eyes before I spin more runs.

aj: Can you paste the command you used and the kernel selection trace?

maria: Sure — command was: ```./tools/run_rope_sweep.sh --models llm3-8b,mistral-7b,mixtral-8x,qwen-7b --modes linear,ntk,yarn --scales 0.8,1.0,1.2,1.4,1.6 --longctx 8192,16384,32768 --batch 4```

maria: Short table (model | variant | scale | qps | p99(ms) | ppl_delta | kernel_choice):
Mistral-7B | linear | 1.0 | 420 | 32 | +0.0 | headslice_v2
Mixtral-8x | NTK | 1.4 | 240 | 78 | +2.3 | fallback_gemm (slow path)
Llama-3-8B | YARN | 1.6 | 310 | 45 | +0.5 | headkv_opt
Qwen-7B | NTK | 1.2 | 360 | 38 | +0.8 | headslice_v2

maria: Observations: Mixtral + NTK >1.2 triggers kernel selector fallback to fallback_gemm; that's the regression in both latency and perplexity. Also saw a correlated drop in KV hit rate before perplexity spikes.

perf-bot: nightly profile snapshot attached: GPU mem 88%, GPU util 76%, avg kernel switch count 3.2, top kernels: headslice_v2 (48%), fallback_gemm (22%), headkv_opt (18%). KV hit ratio over last 5k requests: 0.914 -> 0.872 when spike occurs.

kai: This smells like two related issues: 1) kernel selector's head-dim divisibility check rejects optimized kernels for certain headkv dims when scaled (NTK alters effective rotary freq -> shifted mod). 2) KV cache eviction pattern: batching + longctx sometimes evicts head slices out of the cache leading to worse attention state and ppl regression.

nate: For Mixtral specifically, head-kv dims aren't canonical multiples of 64 after some quantized packing. If the selector enforces mod8/mod16 guards we will hit fallback_gemm. We should consider relaxing the check to test headslice_v2 even if dims % 8 != 0 (with a soft guard and perf telemetry).

olivia: I can run a forced-kernel pass. Will try: ```REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=headslice_v2 ./tools/run_rope_sweep.sh --model mixtral-8x --mode ntk --scale 1.4 --longctx 8192 --batch 2``` — will report back on ppl and mem.

maria: Perfect — FYI I also repro'd longctx instability at 32k: with NTK scale >1.4 we see perplexity climb after ~600 tokens into prefix-heavy sequences. With forced headslice_v2, ppl recovers to within +0.3 but QPS drops ~6% and GPU mem +4%.

aj: Can you attach a kernel selection trace (just the sequence of decisions) and the small profiler flame for the failing run? That helps us decide selector heuristics to change.

maria: Attached inline snippet from selector log: ```[selector] model=mixtral-8x scale=1.4 head_dim=76 try=headslice_v2 -> reject (mod_check fail) try=headkv_opt -> accept try=fallback_gemm -> chosen```

kai: Good catch — head_dim=76 is the culprit. Two paths: (A) change selector to attempt headslice_v2 heuristically when head_dim in {76,92,100} (observed set), collect perf telemetry; (B) implement a head-slice adapter that pads or shards headkv state to compatible dims at runtime (more invasive). Start with (A).

nate: Also let's record KV hit ratio with a fine-grained window during longctx runs. If hit ratio dips below 0.90 consistently before ppl spike, we can tie an automatic reduce-scale fallback to preserve quality.

olivia: Run results: forced headslice_v2 -> ppl delta +0.3, p99 down from 78ms -> 62ms (better), QPS +15% relative to fallback_gemm path, GPU mem +4%. So headslice_v2 is actually better for quality and latency once it can run. Cost is memory.

maria: I'll open an experiment ticket and a selector change PR. Proposal: selector change (soft-allow for non-mod-headdims), and a runtime metric gate: only soft-allow if GPU mem < 92% and KV_hit_ratio > 0.90. If mem or KV hit bad, fall back to fallback_gemm. Also add telemetry for 'selector_soft_allow' cases.

aj: Sounds good. Please include a small canary on dedicated capacity so we don't hit hosted customers.

maria: Done — ticket INF-1452: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1452 (selector soft-allow + telemetry). Assigned to @kai and @olivia. Running canary now on dedicated pool.

kai: thumbs up :thumbsup:

maria: Will post result summary once canary finishes (~2h). Thanks all.
